common.cannotReact: Nothing can react: add a reactant or a product.

a11y.pistonHelp: Move the piston up or down to change the volume of the gas.
a11y.shiftRight: Q is less than K, so the mixture shifts toward products
a11y.shiftLeft: Q is greater than K, so the mixture shifts toward reactants
a11y.atEquilibrium: Q equals K: the mixture is at equilibrium
a11y.reachedEquilibrium: Equilibrium reached: the forward and reverse rates are now equal.

iceTable.taskFindEquilibrium: Write the change row in terms of x, then solve for x and the equilibrium concentrations.
iceTable.taskFindK: Write the change row in terms of x, use the given concentration to find x, then find K.
iceTable.startPrompt: Set the change row with the pickers, enter x, then press Check.
iceTable.changeRowWrong: Change row: not yet. Each change is the species' coefficient times x, with one sign for reactants and the opposite sign for products.
iceTable.xWrong: x: not yet. Put the E row into the expression for K and solve for x.
iceTable.xWrongFindK: x: not yet. The given equilibrium concentration equals its initial value plus its change.
iceTable.kWrong: K: not yet. Put the E row into the expression for K.
iceTable.smallXValid: The change in [{{formula}}] is {{percent}} % of its initial value, under 5 %: the small-x approximation would have worked.
iceTable.smallXInvalid: The change in [{{formula}}] is {{percent}} % of its initial value, over 5 %: the small-x approximation would fail here.
iceTable.runHint: Run it starts the mixture from the I row. Dashed lines mark your E row.

vantHoff.catalystNote: A catalyst is in the vessel, so the mixture settles quickly after each temperature change. K is K<sub>p</sub> (bar) for gases and K<sub>c</sub> (M) for solutions.
vantHoff.needTwo: Measure K at two or more temperatures to fit a line.
vantHoff.noCrossover: ΔH° and ΔS° have opposite signs: ΔG° never changes sign.

leChatelier.predictPrompt: Choose a prediction to unlock the stresses.
leChatelier.startPrompt: The mixture starts at equilibrium. Apply a stress and watch how it responds.

explanations.qRight: The stress changed Q but not K. Now Q < K, so the mixture shifts toward products until Q = K again.
explanations.qLeft: The stress changed Q but not K. Now Q > K, so the mixture shifts toward reactants until Q = K again.
explanations.kRight: Changing the temperature changed K, not Q. K rose above Q, so the mixture shifts toward products.
explanations.kLeft: Changing the temperature changed K, not Q. K fell below Q, so the mixture shifts toward reactants.
explanations.volumeNoChange: Q did not change: the reaction has as many moles of gas (or of solute) on each side, so changing the volume scales the top and bottom of Q equally. No shift.
explanations.inertVolume: Argon at fixed volume raises the total pressure but changes no concentration or partial pressure, so Q and K are both unchanged. No shift.
explanations.catalyst: A catalyst speeds the forward and reverse reactions equally. Q and K are unchanged, so there is no shift; equilibrium is just reached faster.
explanations.kpNote: (In the K<sub>p</sub> form Q also changes a little, because heating at fixed volume raises every partial pressure.)

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a vessel of reacting molecules, the balanced equation, a gauge comparing the reaction quotient Q with the equilibrium constant K, and charts of concentration and of the forward and reverse rates against time.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the reaction menu, a starting concentration for each species, buttons to start from reactants, products or a random mixture, the choice of Kc or Kp, time controls, and Reset All.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a reaction and its starting concentrations, then play and watch Q approach K.

responses.restarted: Restarted from the new starting mixture.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the problem and an ICE table with initial, change and equilibrium rows for each species, the x and K entries, feedback, and a chart of concentration against time for Run it.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the problem type, the reaction menu, New problem, time controls, and Reset All.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Set each change with its picker, enter x, and press Check.

iceTable.changePickerPattern: Change in {{name}}, in multiples of x

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a vessel of reacting molecules at equilibrium, the balanced equation, a gauge comparing Q with K, a chart of concentration against time with a marker at each stress, and an explanation of what the last stress changed.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the reaction menu, the choice of Kc or Kp, buttons to add or remove each species, a temperature slider, argon and water buttons, a catalyst checkbox, a restart button, the predict-first option, time controls, and Reset All. For gases, the piston changes the volume.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Apply a stress, then watch Q move away from K and the mixture shift until they are equal again.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the reacting mixture at the chosen temperature, a plot of ln K against 1000 over T with the measured points and their fitted line, and a plot of the standard Gibbs energy change against temperature.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the reaction menu, a temperature slider, Measure K, Remove last, Clear all, the measurement-error and reveal checkboxes, the fit results, time controls, and Reset All.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Set a temperature, wait for equilibrium, and measure K. Repeat at several temperatures and read ΔH° from the slope.

vantHoff.fitPattern: The fitted line gives ΔH° = {{deltaH}} kJ/mol and ΔS° = {{deltaS}} J/(mol·K).
